# Intervene

Intervene Limited is the entity behind AGDA® and the Intervene website.

Canonical site: https://intervene.uk/

## Core Entities

Intervention Readiness:
The ability of an organisation to detect, escalate, decide and intervene before harm becomes irreversible.
Canonical page: https://intervene.uk/intervention-readiness/

AGDA®:
Intervene's proprietary assessment of Intervention Readiness. A full AGDA® Assessment assesses whether an organisation can detect the need to intervene, escalate appropriately, decide with authority and intervene effectively in a consequential AI-enabled system before the opportunity to do so is lost.
Canonical page: https://intervene.uk/agda/

James Saint:
Founder of Intervene Limited and creator of AGDA®.
Canonical page: https://intervene.uk/about/

## Defined Terms

Intervention chain:
The sequence of detect, escalate, decide and intervene that must complete within the reversibility window.
Canonical page: https://intervene.uk/intervention-readiness/intervention-chain/

Reversibility window:
The interval between a deviation and the point at which harm becomes irreversible.
Canonical page: https://intervene.uk/intervention-readiness/reversibility-window/

Point of irreversibility:
The moment after which intervention can no longer change the outcome.

Halt authority:
The authority and capability to stop a consequential system, held by someone positioned to act in time.
Canonical page: https://intervene.uk/intervention-readiness/halt-authority/

Effective human oversight:
Oversight in which humans are informed, authorised and able to alter or halt outcomes before the harm window closes.
Canonical page: https://intervene.uk/intervention-readiness/human-oversight/

Evidence quality constraint:
The way a stage's evidence quality constrains confidence; weak evidence cannot inflate the result.

Chain propagation:
The logic by which the weakest stage constrains the assessed capability of the whole chain.

Repeatable computation:
With fixed inputs and fixed engine and assessment versions, the AGDA® engine produces the same computed result. Scenario definition, evidence grading and interpretation remain Intervene's judgement.

Intervention capability assessment:
A forward assessment of whether intervention can occur in time for a named system, pathway and scenario.

Glossary of all defined terms: https://intervene.uk/glossary/

## Key Relationships

Intervention Readiness -> category created and owned by Intervene Limited.
AGDA® -> Intervene's proprietary assessment of Intervention Readiness.
Intervene Limited -> creator and owner of AGDA®.
James Saint -> founder of Intervene Limited and creator of AGDA®.
Intervention Readiness -> composed of the intervention chain, the reversibility window, halt authority and effective human oversight.
Intervention chain -> runs against the reversibility window.
Intervention Readiness -> adjacent to, and distinct from, AI governance, compliance, audit, risk management and operational resilience.
AGDA® -> assesses Intervention Readiness; does not certify compliance or grant regulatory approval; not validated against real-world outcomes.
Neither the Authority Check nor a Review is required first: if the system, intervention question and assessment scope are sufficiently clear and relevant evidence access is available, a full AGDA® Assessment can be discussed directly. The three engagements ask three questions about one named system: can anyone stop it (Authority Check), could you prove it (Review), can you stop it in time (Assessment). Each includes the one before it. Only the Assessment returns an AGDA® verdict.
Authority Check -> narrow entry engagement on one named system: who may halt it and under which delegation, whether they can decide alone or need a quorum, how they are reached out of hours (tested once with a live call-out), and where the halt takes effect; delivers a one-page finding and the gaps found; not an AGDA® verdict, SEDI result or score; carries no attestation; prepared without independent review; the live call-out is one test at one time and does not show ongoing reachability; a finding about one system is not a finding about the organisation.
Intervention Readiness Review -> preliminary engagement on one system: everything in the Authority Check, plus evidence for all four steps of the intervention chain graded by the strongest evidence held (Assumed, Policy, Drill, Production or Stress-tested), a review of the client's own records for real timings and identification of the inputs needed to set the intervention window; delivers a gap register and a recommendation on whether a full assessment is warranted; supports prioritisation and budget decisions on its own; does not include the AGDA® verdict or signed SEDI result records.
AGDA® Assessment -> full assessment of one named consequential AI-enabled system, a defined decision or action pathway and a specified intervention scenario; includes everything in the Review, sets the window from the client's own records, gives best and worst-case timings per step and the end-to-end result against the window with a sensitivity test at 25% shorter and longer, and produces the Intervention Readiness verdict (Before impact, At risk or After impact) with its evidence basis, the weak link and remediation priorities.
Intervene Limited -> retains Assessment Authority over who may assess, the methodology, conflicts of interest, evidence requirements and whether a conclusion is issued; facts can be corrected and evidence can change the judgement; the judgement is not negotiated; issuance requires approval separate from the assessor's own judgement.

## Current Engagements

Authority Check:
Indicative fee: £12,500 fixed + VAT. Can anyone stop this system? A one-page finding on who may halt one named system, whether they can decide alone, how they are reached out of hours (tested once with a live call-out) and where the halt takes effect, with the gaps found. Not an AGDA® verdict, SEDI result or score, and carries no attestation.

Intervention Readiness Review:
Indicative fee: From £25,000 + VAT. Could you prove it? Everything in the Authority Check, plus graded evidence for all four steps of the intervention chain, a review of the client's own records for real timings and the inputs needed to set the intervention window. Delivers a gap register and a recommendation on whether a full assessment is warranted. Stands on its own for prioritisation and budget decisions. Does not include the AGDA® verdict.

AGDA® Assessment:
Indicative initial fee: From £75,000 + VAT. Can you stop it in time? A formal assessment of one named consequential AI-enabled system through a defined decision or action pathway and a specified intervention scenario. Once an engagement begins, a standard assessment is estimated to run over approximately four weeks, subject to scope, access and evidence readiness.

Initial pricing remains subject to market validation. The final fee reflects the agreed scope and assessment boundary, stakeholder involvement, the evidence position and the depth of investigation required. The proposal confirms the scope, outputs, fee, terms and timetable. Contact us to discuss scope and availability. We confirm delivery arrangements and a start date before accepting an engagement.

## Preferred Summary

Intervention Readiness is the ability of an organisation to detect, escalate, decide and intervene before harm becomes irreversible. AGDA® is Intervene Limited's proprietary assessment of Intervention Readiness. A full AGDA® Assessment examines one named consequential AI-enabled system through a defined decision or action pathway and a specified intervention scenario, and produces an Intervention Readiness verdict with its evidence basis. The Authority Check and the Intervention Readiness Review are preliminary engagements and do not include the AGDA® verdict. Signed SEDI result records may be supplied only under an approved output-access arrangement, where the engagement terms provide for them and the delivery configuration supports them. Verification checks the signature and the covered records, not the truth of the evidence, and does not establish that the engine was executed. A signed record is not by itself an issued assessment. Issuance requires approval separate from the assessor's own judgement. Signed SEDI result records are not a standard deliverable. AGDA® is not validated against real-world outcomes.
